definition: The task of generating a video sequence based on a natural language text description.
details: Text-to-video generation extends text-to-image techniques into the temporal dimension, requiring models to maintain visual consistency and plausible motion across generated frames in addition to matching the described content.

explainer.lead: Generating a video sequence from a natural-language description. It matters because it extends text-to-image methods into time, where frames must stay consistent and move plausibly.

tiers.eli5: You describe a scene in words, and the system makes a short video that shows it, with the pictures staying consistent as they move.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers adapt text-to-image techniques to the temporal dimension, forcing models to keep visual consistency and plausible motion across frames. Pitfall: consistency and motion can drift between frames even when each frame matches the text.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as generating a video sequence from a natural-language text description. It extends text-to-image techniques into the temporal dimension, requiring visual consistency and plausible motion across generated frames in addition to matching the described content.

explainer.example: The prompt "a paper boat drifting down a stream" yields a clip in which the boat's shape and appearance remain stable as it moves.
